stem: In a circuit, $L$, $C$ and $R$ are connected in series with an alternating voltage source of frequency $f$. The current leads the voltage by $45^\circ$. The value of $C$ is
solution:
$\tan45^\circ = \dfrac{\frac{1}{\omega C} - \omega L}{R} \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{\omega C} = R + \omega L$

$C = \dfrac{1}{\omega(R + \omega L)} = \dfrac{1}{2\pi f(R + 2\pi fL)}$

An ideal black body at room temperature is thrown into a furnace. It is observed that
options: Initially it is the darkest body and at later times the brightest
It is the darkest body at all times
It cannot be distinguished at all times
Initially it is the darkest body and at later times it cannot be distinguished
solution: Initially the black body absorbs all radiation incident on it, so it is the darkest. A black body radiates maximum energy under the same conditions, so when it reaches the furnace temperature it is the brightest.
